new_statements.quote: El patrón de acentuación en todas las variantes del idioma kaqchikel es fijo, su función es demarcativa y su posición es en sílaba final (acento agudo o último). Es invariable en el proceso de derivación. Por eso, no es necesaria su escritura, porque es predecible y no ejerce función distintiva.
new_statements.translation: The stress pattern in all varieties of the Kaqchikel language is fixed, its function is demarcative and its position is on the final syllable (acute or last-syllable stress). It is invariant in the process of derivation. For that reason it need not be written, because it is predictable and has no distinctive function.
new_statements.citation: Comunidad Lingüística Kaqchikel (ALMG); Ajsivinac Sián, J. E., Lolmay P. O. García Mátzar, M. Chacach Cutzal & I. E. Alonzo Guaján. 2004. Gramática descriptiva del idioma maya Kaqchikel: Rutzijoxik rucholik ri Kaqchikel ch'ab'äl. Chimaltenango: Comunidad Lingüística Kaqchikel, Academia de Lenguas Mayas de Guatemala.
new_statements.locator: Fonología, section 'Acento', printed p. 55 (p. 59); exceptions pp. 56-57
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (216 pp., archive.org scan; the embedded text is garbage, so I read the held page render and independently re-rendered p.59 with page render, which is the same page: printed p.55, header FONOLOGÍA, section 'Acento'). The quoted passage is there word for word: 'El patrón de acentuación en todas las variantes del idioma kaqchikel es fijo, su función es demarcativa y su posición es en sílaba final (acento agudo o último). Es invariable en el proceso de derivación. Por eso, no es necesaria su escritura, porque es predecible y no ejerce función distintiva.' followed by underlined final-syllable examples (nupatz'an, patän, kumätz, tukur..) and fn. 48 'Datos de la Variación Dialectal del Id…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress falls on the last syllable of the word in every Kaqchikel variety, including after derivational suffixation; it is predictable and non-contrastive. The independent OKMA grammar (García Matzar & Rodríguez Guaján 1997, p. 20) states the same rule ('acento fijo.. agudo.. siempre.. en la sílaba final de la palabra') and adds that directional enclitics on verbs/statives attract the stress.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in ALMG 2004 or OKMA 1997; Bennett 2018 (Glossa, fn. 7) states secondary stress has never been reported for Kaqchikel and there is no phonotactic evidence for it.
new_statements.exceptions: ALMG 2004 p. 56: penultimate stress in a few native words (vakix 'cow', tukur 'owl', tata, nana, b'alam, anxa, janila 'very') and Spanish loans (anma, paxa, alb'ertix, xalma); 'acento en sílaba pesada' (first vowel followed by glottal stop in transitive verb forms) in very few words only in Santa María de Jesús, Antigua, Parramos, San Bartolomé and Magdalena Milpas Altas, plus diphthong loans in Santa María de Jesús/Alotenango (p. 57). Yepocapa is not named among the exception varieties. OKMA 1997 p. 21 adds nana/tata, Comalapa janila, Tecpán b'ala.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (root, derived and compound words); enclitics (directionals) attach and take the stress. The statement is Kaqchikel-language-level ('en todas las variantes'); the grammar's dialect data (CLK Informe de Variación Dialectal) include San Pedro Yepocapa (printed pp. 34, 40, 155, 161), but no Yepocapa-specific stress data are given.
new_statements.identity_note: kaqc1271 is a Glottolog bookkeeping code: ISO [cbm] 'Yepocapa Southwestern Cakchiquel' was merged into Kaqchikel [cak] (kaqc1270) by ISO CR 2008-053, effective 2009-01-16. Ethnologue 15 located it in the municipio of (San Pedro) Yepocapa, 8,000 speakers (1991 SIL), all over 40. No Yepocapa-specific phonological description exists; the statement quoted is Kaqchikel-language-level from the ALMG descriptive grammar, which asserts it 'en todas las variantes' and whose CLK dialect-survey data explicitly include San Pedro Yepocapa (printed pp. 34, 40, 155, 161 incl. a Yepocapa text 'YEP'). The only Yepocapa-specific primary material found is Kaufman's 1970 PLFM dialect-survey questionnaire (handwritten wordlist, no stress prose). Any catalog entry should be filed under kaqc1270 (Kaqchikel) with Yepocapa noted as a covered variety, not as a separate language.

sources.note: p.55 'Acento': stress pattern in ALL variants of Kaqchikel is fixed, demarcative, on the final syllable (acento agudo), invariant under derivation, not. p.56: penultimate stress in a few native words (vakix, tukur, tata, nana, b'alam, anxa, janila) and Spanish loans (anma, paxa, alb'ertix, xalma); 'acento en sílaba pesada' in very few words only in Santa María de Jesús, Antigua, Parramos, San Bartolomé and Magdalena Milpas Altas (p.56-57; Alotenango diphthong loans) -- Yepocapa not among those exceptions, but its data are in the CLK survey (pp. 34, 40, 155, 161).

sources.citation: Bennett, Ryan. 2018. Recursive prosodic words in Kaqchikel (Mayan). Glossa 3(1): 67. doi:10.5334/gjgl.550
sources.note: pp.11-12: stress 'basically restricted to word-final position'; fn.7: 'Secondary stress has never been reported for Kaqchikel', no phonotactic evidence for it. Language-level (Comalapa/Sololá varieties), not Yepocapa.

sources.citation: Bennett, Ryan. 2016. Mayan phonology. Language and Linguistics Compass 10(10): 469-514. doi:10.1111/lnc3.12148
sources.note: sec. 6.1 (p.495): 'Final stress (36a) is the norm in K'ichean languages'; 'Kaqchikel.. follows the typical K'ichean pattern of final stress, but non-final stress occurs in both loanwords (anima) and in some native words (janila)'. Survey, language-level.

sources.citation: García Matzar, Pedro (Lolmay) & José Obispo Rodríguez Guaján (Pakal B'alam). 1997 [1a reimpr. 2001]. Rukemik ri Kaqchikel chi': Gramática kaqchikel. Guatemala: Cholsamaj / OKMA.
sources.note: p.20: 'El Kaqchikel se caracteriza por tener acento fijo en una sílaba determinada. El acento es agudo, lo que significa que la acentuación siempre va a recaer en la sílaba final de la palabra (radical, derivada o compuesta..)'; enclitics on verbs/statives attract stress; p.21: Spanish loans keep penult/antepenult stress (kaxa, xara, anma); native exceptions nana, tata; Comalapa janila; Iximche' b'ala. Authors' own dialects are Tecpán and San Andrés Semetabaj, not Yepocapa.

sources.citation: Berinstein, Ava E. 1979. A cross-linguistic study on the perception and production of stress. UCLA Working Papers in Phonetics 47.
sources.note: abstract/p.3: 'Both K'ekchi and Cakchiquel have fixed final stress'; Cakchiquel subjects were students from Patzicía, not Yepocapa.
